gloss: New Year's greeting; Happy New Year

definitions.gloss: New Year's greeting; Happy New Year
definitions.explanation: A formal expression used on New Year's cards and decorations to celebrate the new year. Literally means 'celebrating the new year.' Primarily a written greeting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{賀正|がしょう}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote 'Happy New Year' on the New Year's card.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{賀正|がしょう}」⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}ていた→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: A New Year's decoration saying 'Happy New Year' was displayed at the company entrance.
It's better not to use 'gashou' on New Year's cards to people of higher status.

notes:
USAGE:
{賀正|がしょう} is a two-character New Year's greeting commonly printed on ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧ (New Year's cards) and seasonal decorations. It is considered a somewhat casual abbreviated form.

IMPORTANT: Two-character greetings like {賀正|がしょう} are traditionally seen as abbreviated and therefore less formal. When writing to superiors or elders, four-character greetings such as ⟦{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}→謹賀新年：17279_kingashinnen⟧ are preferred.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {賀正|がしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧ (New Year's greeting decoration)
- ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{賀正|がしょう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (write 'gashou' on a New Year's card)

RELATED WORDS:
